input.quote: In the event that SFJ terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 14.2.1 then in exchange for purchasing the Trial Data Package including the Research Results included therein as set forth in Section 11.1.1.4, PB will pay SFJ, within [***] of the date of termination, an amount equal to three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination.
input.rationale: Section 14.2.1 requires PB (our party) to pay SFJ 300% of all Development Costs paid or incurred if SFJ terminates for PB's uncured material breach, and Section 14.4.2 expressly states that the amounts payable on a given termination are "in lieu of any claim for damages" — i.e., a breach-triggered liquidated sum payable by the customer. A treble multiple of amounts funded is far beyond the fallback (a single, capped early-termination amount) and is punitive rather than compensatory, so it fails the fallback on a material term. Our minimal edit strips only the 300% multiplier, leaving PB to repay the Development Costs actually funded, consistent with Section 14.2.9 (Adverse Patent Impact), which is set at all Development Costs paid or incurred. We have not flagged the 300% at-will amount in Section 14.2.2 or the 150% change-of-control amount in Section 14.2.6, which are addressed under the termination-for-convenience and assignment rules; the parallel 300% amounts in Sections 14.2.5.2 and 14.2.7 and the 25% interest add-on in Section 14.2.10 should be conformed if this change is accepted. Section 14.4.2's cap on SFJ's damages claim benefits us and is not challenged.

proposal.summary: Remove the 300% penalty multiplier on the breach-triggered termination payment in Section 14.2.1 so PB repays Development Costs actually funded.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the 300% multiplier so that, if SFJ terminates for our material breach, we repay the Development Costs SFJ actually paid or incurred rather than three times that amount; a treble, breach-triggered payment that Section 14.4.2 treats as being in lieu of damages is a penalty we cannot accept. This also aligns with Section 14.2.9, where the payment equals all Development Costs paid or incurred.

ops.newText: an amount equal to the Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination
